text:
raul: Quick follow-up on the cold-tier demotion idea I brought up last week. Thinking about adding a soft quota + demotion pipeline instead of immediate eviction. Want to align on signal semantics between scheduler <-> allocator.

sophia: I like soft quotas. Can you sketch the lifecycle? e.g., when does an allocation get tagged for demotion vs evict?

raul: Draft flow: 1) allocation ages + low access => mark as COLD. 2) if global free < soft_threshold -> attempt demote (move to host staging compressed). 3) if free still < hard_threshold -> evict. Demote is non-blocking and can be reversed on access.

mike: Important: demotion must be fast to avoid stall on miss. We should avoid copying if possible. Maybe reference-counted remote pages + mmap-backed shims so we can remap cheaply.

jen: Agree on remap approach. But that needs coordination with our kernel shim for on-demand page fault handling. We'd need a small header per page with state: HOT/COOL/COLD/REMOTE.

ingrid: How do tenants factor? If tenant A triggers demote a lot, we shouldn't starve others. Need tenant-aware soft quota windows and a backpressure signal to request routers.

raul: Exactly. Proposal: per-tenant soft_quota and system soft pool. When tenant exceeds soft_quota we emit a "tenant_demote_recommendation" metric and a backpressure token to the request scheduler which can reduce batch sizes or route to cheaper models.

mike: What about fragmentation? Demoting scattered pages could increase host-side fragmentation and page churn. Maybe group candidate pages by arena and only demote if contiguous run >= N pages.

sophia: Good point. Heuristic: only demote runs > 4 pages or pages with similar liveness profiles. Also consider a compaction pass that runs opportunistically when system idle to coalesce.

jen: Can we have a swapless mode for on-prem where demotion uses a preallocated host staging pool (fast-mmap) and we don't rely on system swap? That helps determinism.

raul: Yes, default behavior: swapless demote -> host-staging pool (compressed). Fallback: system swap if staging is full and policy allows.

evict-bot: NOTE: demo config uploaded to staging: `rbw config set allocator.demote.enabled true` (deployed at 3123456800)

ingrid: Ops question: how do we surface demote costs to billing/telemetry? Need token-level accounting: tokens moved * bytes * demote_cost_unit.

mike: Implementation detail: demote should keep a small shadow KV-cache of hot keys to avoid remap on tiny lookups. If hit in shadow, we re-promote async.

sophia: Also add a fail-open flag so if demote fails we don't block inference: prefer to return degraded-latency rather than OOM.

raul: Next steps: I'll write a short RFC with APIs: `Allocator.mark_cold(addr)`, `Allocator.query_candidate_runs()`, `Allocator.demote_run(run_id)`, plus scheduler hooks for backpressure. Will post draft by EOD tomorrow.

jen: Thanks, will review. also ping storage team about compact-on-idle integration.

ingrid: FYI I'll start a telemetry ticket for tenant_demote_recommendation metrics.

mike: quick perf note: add a microbenchmark for remap vs memcpy demote paths.

raul: ack. If no objections I'll open the RFC tomorrow and tag eng-sre + infra. :thumbsup:
